findings.title: apply_atrium_merge per-row write passes engine_internal frame — sync-merged peer writes BYPASS WriteBoundaryChainValidator structurally even when installed
findings.site: crates/benten-engine/src/engine_diagnostics.rs:532-536 (append_version) called from crates/benten-engine/src/engine.rs:1664 (apply_atrium_merge per-row merge Version Node mint)
findings.doc_claim_contradicted: crates/benten-engine/src/engine.rs:2049-2050 — `User-facing CRUD entry points / delegation / sync-merge can present a chain anchor when one is in scope.` (the docstring explicitly names sync-merge as a chain-bearing site)
findings.threat_model: Sync-merged writes are the highest-leverage adversarial surface in Phase-3+ untrusted-peer scenarios — a peer presenting a CRDT op-log row that lands as a Version Node passes through admit_write_chain with engine_internal frame, which short-circuits at engine.rs:2064-2070 (chain_anchor_cid=None -> Ok(())). The Layer-1 user-as-root invariant (CLAUDE.md baked-in #18) is structurally NOT enforced for inbound sync writes even when a substantive WriteBoundaryChainValidator is installed. Per-row cap-recheck at engine.rs:1291+ still fires (defends against revoked actor), but the cap-rooted-chain check is absent.
findings.fix_now_shape: Thread an Atrium-anchored chain frame at the apply_atrium_merge per-row site: derive chain_anchor_cid from the seed's peer-attribution + actor_did from the resolved peer_did, then call append_version with a new transactional path that takes a WriteAdmissionFrame (or add an `append_version_with_chain` shim that admits a non-engine-internal frame). Estimated LOC: ~80-120 + 2-3 test pins.
findings.defer_named_now_destination: If FIX-NOW is out of R6 R2 scope, add NEW Row D-N to docs/V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md (sibling of Row D-1) naming `apply_atrium_merge chain-bearing WriteAdmissionFrame` as the G-COMP-1 destination, AND retense the Row D-1 CLOSED narrative + engine.rs:2049-2050 docstring to remove the sync-merge claim so the doc no longer contradicts the code.

findings.title: D-1 CLOSED narrative in V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md overclaims structural-always-on Layer-1 enforcement — 12 of 13 admit_write_chain sites pass engine_internal frame and unconditionally admit
findings.code_quote: Layer-1 user-as-root invariant is structurally enforced at every WRITE admission when a production validator is installed.
findings.doc_claim_contradicted: Per workspace grep, 12 of 13 admit_write_chain sites pass `WriteAdmissionFrame::engine_internal()`. The helper at engine.rs:2061-2070 short-circuits when chain_anchor_cid is None. Only crates/benten-engine/src/engine_caps.rs:629 (delegate_capability) presents a chain-bearing frame. Layer-1 fires at the delegation-cap-mint entry point ONLY; all other WRITE entry points collapse to NotApplicable.
findings.threat_model: v1-beta-security-claim-honesty cluster (L2-R6-MAJOR-3 shape at R6 R1). A reader of V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md would conclude Layer-1 is comprehensively enforced post-FP-F4; the truth is that the interface is uniformly mounted but the enforcement surface is structurally narrow.
findings.fix_now_shape: Retense docs/V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md Row D-1 CLOSED narrative to: `Layer-1 fires at the delegation-cap-mint entry point (engine_caps::EngineCapsHandle::delegate_capability); all other WRITE entry points (engine_crud CRUD x5 + engine_modules install/uninstall x2 + engine_views x1 + engine_diagnostics x1 + engine_wait x1 + handler_versions x1 + engine_caps privileged_put_node x1 = 12 sites) pass WriteAdmissionFrame::engine_internal and collapse to NotApplicable. Full Layer-1 enforcement across the non-delegation WRITE surface (including apply_atrium_merge per-row, the highest-leverage adversarial site) is the G-COMP-1 cascade — see new Row D-N for apply_atrium_merge chain-bearing wiring.` Same retense at SECURITY-POSTURE.md Compromise #26 v1-beta-posture summary. Estimated LOC: ~25 in 2 docs.

findings.title: §S1 regression-guard test `workspace_walker_audit_thirteen_admit_write_chain_call_sites` is paper-only and cannot detect site-revert regressions
findings.doc_claim_contradicted: Same file's module docstring (lines 18-22): `§3.5n orchestrator ground-truth-verify shape — Each enumerated site has a corresponding admit_write_chain( grep-hit in production code; reverting any one site removes the grep-hit + breaks Layer-1 enforcement at that boundary.` The test claims to be a ground-truth-verify shape but exercises no ground-truth check.
findings.threat_model: META #707 asymmetric-at-parallel-entry-points class: revert detection at 13 distributed sites requires a centralized assertion. The current test passes irrespective of code state (13 == 13 always). A regression that drops one admit_write_chain call would land green CI.
findings.fix_now_shape: Replace the paper assertion with a real workspace walker — `let admit_call_count = std::process::Command::new("grep").args(["-rE", "admit_write_chain\\(", "crates/benten-engine/src/"]).output()...count_lines()...; assert_eq!(admit_call_count, EXPECTED_WRITE_SITES_PER_F1_PATH_A);` — OR commit to a const-string-array enumeration of (file, line-anchor-pattern) pairs that the test walks. Either shape catches reverts. Estimated LOC: ~30-50 in the same test file.

findings.title: Engine WRITE pathways never populate WriteContext::namespace_did — cross-DID storage partition (G-CORE-1 #989) is consumer-unwired at the engine layer at v1-beta; gap not named in V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED
findings.site: Workspace grep `grep -rn namespace_did crates/benten-engine/src/` returns ZERO hits. The substrate (crates/benten-graph/src/redb_backend.rs::put_node_with_context honors namespace_did; crates/benten-graph/src/browser_backend.rs fail-closes on Some) is structurally real but no engine WRITE call site populates namespace_did=Some(did).
findings.doc_claim_contradicted: docs/SECURITY-POSTURE.md:1916-1932 describes the storage-partition mechanism + claims `the cross-DID non-leak invariant ... holds structurally`. The mechanism IS real; what's missing is engine-side adoption. SECURITY-POSTURE.md does NOT explicitly state `at v1-beta no engine WRITE populates namespace_did so all engine writes land in the un-namespaced default partition`. Honest by omission, but the reader could conclude partition isolation is live; it is structurally inert at the consumer layer.
findings.threat_model: Substrate-frozen-but-consumer-unwired pattern (the same shape as the WriteBoundaryChainValidator path before F4). The Principal primitive authority-half (per CLAUDE.md baked-in #18 amendment 2026-05-18) is paper-only at v1-beta — multi-tenancy isolation depends on CapabilityPolicy gating alone, which only binds a cooperating engine (not the Phase-7 untrusted-host / peers-hold-ciphertext threat model the docs name).
findings.fix_now_shape: Add NEW Row D-N to docs/V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md naming `engine-side namespace_did population at WRITE entry points` as a G-COMP-1 destination. Wave brief: thread the engine's principal-DID through WriteContext at every engine_crud + engine_modules + engine_caps + engine_diagnostics + engine_wait write site (the same 13-site cascade F4 just landed for admit_write_chain). Also add a one-sentence v1-beta-posture clarification at SECURITY-POSTURE.md:1916-1932: `At v1-beta no engine WRITE call site populates namespace_did; all engine writes land in the default un-namespaced partition. The substrate is verified end-to-end (RedbBackend / BrowserBackend) but engine-side consumer wiring is the G-COMP-1 deliverable per Row D-N.`

findings.title: audience_did=None at all 3 check_write_with_audience call sites — audience-binding gate is structurally inert at every WRITE consultation
findings.doc_claim_contradicted: ALREADY DISCLOSED at docs/V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md:167-175 Row D-3-c PARTIAL CLOSED narrative + SECURITY-POSTURE.md:2114-2116. The rationale `peer_did at apply_atrium_merge is transport-principal NOT cap-target` is plausibly defensible (cap-target is the resource owner; peer_did is the message sender).
findings.threat_model: The cross-atrium UCAN replay defense (CLR-2 / cap-major-2) requires audience-binding at the per-row cap consultation; passing None makes that defense inert at the cap-recheck site. The Phase-3 G16-B-F per-row cap-recheck still fires + revoked actors still get blocked, but a cross-atrium UCAN whose audience matches a different atrium's audience would not be rejected at the per-row consultation. Per Δv3-2 disposition this is named-deferred to G-COMP-1 + the existing Layer-3 check_per_delegation wiring is argued to cover the delegate-runtime audience-discrimination needs — the case is plausible but not adversarially airtight.
findings.disposition: ALREADY-CLOSED-by-disclosure-in-D-3-c (CARRIED for forensic completeness; no new action)
findings.rationale: Disclosure is honest; the rationale is defensible; the G-COMP-1 destination is named. The CARRIED designation reflects this lens's adversarial obligation to NAME the gap explicitly even when it's already disclosed.

findings.title: install_plugin step 3c discards check_install_consent's actual ErrorCode via `.is_err()` remap to PluginInstallConsentDenied — information loss for incident diagnosis
findings.threat_model: A CapabilityPolicy::check_install_consent impl that returns a typed ErrorCode::Unauthenticated (e.g. user-DID signature failed at the policy's pre-check) gets silently flattened to PluginInstallConsentDenied. The high-level install_plugin caller can't distinguish denied-by-policy from denied-due-to-policy-internal-error.
findings.rationale: The install_plugin entry point IS a high-level surface where the user-facing shape is 'denied'; underlying reasons are still surfacable through policy-side tracing/logging. Acceptable surface posture; not a security gap. Could be improved by preserving the underlying code via map_err(|inner| { tracing::error!(?inner); ErrorCode::PluginInstallConsentDenied }), but no functional change.
